native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: Pottery Decoration and Pottery Form first diverge in the transition from the 18th into the 17th century BCE (between the 1800 BCE and 1700 BCE anchors, ≈3750–3650 calBP), with Pottery Decoration rising by +1.45 z (−0.48→+0.97) while Pottery Form declines by −1.87 z (+0.74→−1.13); this is the first and only century interval in the 4100–500 BCE series with ΔDecoration>0 and ΔForm<0, and it becomes a sustained regime.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Built the century-level series from time_series_data.csv raw anchors (CE=−4100…−500 in strict 100-yr steps, calBP=1950−CE), cross-validated against capital.csv (exact match, max diff 0.0). 2) Growth = first difference in z-units per consecutive century bin. 3) Scanned chronologically for the earliest interval with ΔDecoration>0 AND ΔForm<0. 4) Robustness checks: (a) annual linear-interpolated series — first qualifying year is 1799 BCE, none earlier; (b) sustained regime confirmed (Form −1.13 / Decoration ≥+0.97 for 13-plus anchors; earliest 200-yr opposite net-change window 1900→1700 contains the same transition); (c) capital.csv alone reproduces the identical result. 5) Threshold sensitivity verified identical under |Δ| thresholds 0.0–1.4.
